content.value_statement: Marketing teams can lose track of approved claim wording, offer terms, and supporting evidence. This skill records proposals and accepted records with provenance, disclosures, review dates, and expiry status.
actual_capabilities: Registers claim and offer proposals with exact wording or terms.
Tracks evidence sources, dates, scope, and user-provided provenance.
Records required disclosures, review dates, and offer expiry dates.
Queries current claim and offer projection records by aggregate ID.
Preserves append-only proposal and decision history for accepted records.
limitations: It does not independently verify evidence or provide legal advice.
It does not write advertising copy or approve a concrete advertisement use.
Standalone installs can prepare proposals but cannot claim canonical approval.
It depends on the host registry, event schema, and available source evidence.

use_cases.title: Document a performance claim
use_cases.description: Record exact claim wording, supporting study details, scope, disclosure, and a review date before campaign production.

use_cases.title: Track a seasonal promotion
use_cases.description: Store offer terms, eligibility, destination, start date, end date, and linked claims in one controlled record.

use_cases.title: Resolve missing proof
use_cases.description: Review pending proposals and keep unsupported wording unresolved until a source is supplied.

prompt_templates.title: Register a simple claim
prompt_templates.prompt: Register this claim: "Customers save 20% on annual plans." Evidence: pricing page updated 2026-07-20. Add the applicable disclosure and a review date.

prompt_templates.title: Check an offer
prompt_templates.prompt: Show the current terms, eligibility, destination, and expiry for offer summer-2026. Identify missing fields or unresolved linked claims.

prompt_templates.title: Create an evidence-aware proposal
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a proposal for this claim without approving it: "Reduces setup time by 30%." Evidence is a user-provided spreadsheet dated 2026-07-15. Record its limits and required review.

prompt_templates.title: Review pending records
prompt_templates.prompt: Review pending claim proposals in order. Accept only records with sufficient evidence, preserve unresolved items, and summarize decisions with aggregate IDs and evidence gaps.

output_examples.input: Register a claim for free shipping on orders over $50, valid through August 31.
output: Claim proposal created for the exact free-shipping wording.
Terms include the $50 threshold and August 31 expiry.
Evidence and approval status remain unresolved until reviewed.

output_examples.input: What is the current status of offer summer-2026?
output: Current terms and dates are retrieved from the accepted projection.
The response lists linked claims, required disclosures, and any pending evidence gaps.

best_practices: Provide exact claim wording or complete offer terms before requesting registration.
Attach a dated evidence source and clearly label user-provided information.
Review records before expiry and keep unsupported claims unresolved.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a proposal as approved claim wording.
Do not use user assertions as independent substantiation.
Do not manually edit the event stream or generated ledger views.

faq.question: Does this skill approve advertising claims?
faq.answer: No. It records claim status and evidence provenance. Auditors decide whether a concrete use passes review.

faq.question: Can I register an unsupported claim?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill can create an unresolved proposal and mark missing proof as none-on-file.

faq.question: What evidence should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the source owner, date, scope, population, and limits for the claim or offer.

faq.question: Can it manage offer expiry?
faq.answer: Yes. It records start and end dates and supports dated expiry or withdrawal state changes.

faq.question: Can it edit the claims ledger directly?
faq.answer: No. The ledger is a generated view. Canonical changes use append-only registry events with explicit permission.

faq.question: Does it provide legal advice?
faq.answer: No. It records disclosures and policy sources but does not make legal conclusions.
